# `silk/simd/cpu`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Runtime detection of the CPU features that the running machine has.

## When to use
Use [`CpuFeatures.detect`](#CpuFeatures.impl.detect) when one binary must pick a faster kernel on machines that have a
feature the build does not select. Use `Target.hasCpuFeature` with `static if` when the build
itself selects the feature, which costs nothing at run time.

## Details
A [`CpuFeatures`](#CpuFeatures) value is a set of feature names of the target architecture, spelled as in
the compilation profile, such as `"avx2"`, `"dotprod"` or `"simd128"`. [`CpuFeatures.selected`](#CpuFeatures.impl.selected)
is the set the build selects. [`CpuFeatures.detect`](#CpuFeatures.impl.detect) asks the machine and always includes the
selected set:

- x86-64 reads `cpuid`, and counts AVX and AVX-512 features only when the operating system
  saves their registers (`xgetbv`).
- AArch64 Linux with GNU libc reads `getauxval`. AArch64 Darwin reads `sysctlbyname`.
- wasm32 cannot ask the engine, and other profiles cannot ask the system, so they report
  the selected set.

Silk has no mutable global storage, so detection is not cached. Call `detect` once at start
and keep the value, for example in a service.

## Gotchas
- A name from another architecture, or an unknown name, is never present.
- A detected feature does not make `Target.hasCpuFeature` true. Code that uses the feature's
  instructions must still be compiled for it.

## Examples
### Ask the machine once
```silk
import silk.simd.cpu { CpuFeatures }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let machine = CpuFeatures.detect()
  let build = CpuFeatures.selected()
  // The machine has every feature the build selects.
  if CpuFeatures.has(&build, "sse2") && !CpuFeatures.has(&machine, "sse2") {
    return 1
  }
  if !CpuFeatures.containsAll(&machine, &build) {
    return 1
  }
  if CpuFeatures.has(&machine, "no-such-feature") {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="CpuFeatures.impl.detect"></a>

### Associated function `detect`

```silk
pub fn detect() -> CpuFeatures
```

Returns the features of the running machine, which include [`CpuFeatures.selected`](#CpuFeatures.impl.selected).

#### Details

Each call asks the machine again:

- x86-64 reads `cpuid`, and counts AVX and AVX-512 features only when the operating system
  saves their registers (`xgetbv`).
- AArch64 Linux with GNU libc reads `getauxval`. AArch64 Darwin reads `sysctlbyname`.
- wasm32 cannot ask the engine, and other profiles cannot ask the system, so they report the
  selected set.

Silk has no mutable global storage, so the result is not cached. Call `detect` once at start
and keep the value, for example in a service.

#### Gotchas

A detected feature does not make `Target.hasCpuFeature` true. Code that uses the feature's
instructions must still be compiled for it.

<a id="CpuFeatures.impl.has"></a>

### Method `has`

```silk
pub fn has(self: &Self, name: string) -> bool
```

Returns `true` if the set contains the feature `name`.

<a id="CpuFeatures.impl.containsAll"></a>

### Method `containsAll`

```silk
pub fn containsAll(self: &Self, other: &CpuFeatures) -> bool
```

Returns `true` if the set contains every feature of `other`.
